coverage: Six initial rows carry selected exact normative excerpts. scripts/check_r3v_drm_requirement_sources.py validates pinned source locators, policy references, chapter blob identities, anchor declarations, and excerpt containment between consecutive declarations. docs/r3v-vulkan-normative-sources.md records reproduction and quotation limits. Allocation, image binding, packet grammar, suspend, complete clause coverage, and behavioral qualification remain open.

specification.excerpt:
There must: be at least one memory type with both the
ename:VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT and
ename:VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT bits set in its
pname:propertyFlags.

requirements.requirement: At least one memory type is both HOST_VISIBLE and HOST_COHERENT. Coherent memory requires neither application flush nor application invalidation for the respective host and device writes.
requirements.interface: GEM_CREATE cache attributes, GEM_MMAP, and R3V software cache maintenance
requirements.test: Exercise every native GPU access path with persistently mapped memory and application flush and invalidate calls omitted; verify producer and consumer digests and maintenance ordering through real queue seams, then retain target observations.
requirements.boundary: R3V advertises software-maintained coherence around synchronous submission. Removing HOST_COHERENT alone violates the required memory-type minimum. A kernel cache-attribute change requires evidence that userspace maintenance cannot meet the complete contract.

specification.excerpt:
The pname:size member of the sname:VkMemoryRequirements structure
    returned from a call to fname:vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements with
    pname:buffer must: be less than or equal to the size of pname:memory
    minus pname:memoryOffset

requirements.requirement: A valid buffer binding fits the required byte size within the allocation after the binding offset. Related valid usage requires an allowed memory type and aligned offset.
requirements.interface: VkDeviceMemory GEM BO plus resource offset, translated into packet addresses and relocations
requirements.test: Exercise aligned suballocations, exact-end ranges, multiple resources sharing one allocation, and deliberately invalid range controls through binding and packet construction; qualify parser bounds separately.
requirements.boundary: Vulkan valid usage constrains the application. Mesa owns resource binding semantics; DRM independently contains packet accesses within GEM objects and retains their lifetime.

specification.excerpt:
A _memory dependency_ is an execution dependency which includes availability
and visibility operations such that:

  * The first set of operations happens-before the availability operation.
  * The availability operation happens-before the visibility operation.
  * The visibility operation happens-before the second set of operations.

requirements.requirement: Memory dependencies order operations and include availability and visibility for their access scopes.
requirements.hypothesis: A packet that writes through a relocation declared read-only can receive incomplete reservation dependencies and publish a READ fence. Actual packet role validation must be tested before declaring a demonstrated defect.
requirements.test: Run actual supported packet consumers with accurate and inaccurate access declarations, including duplicate handles; inspect scheduling and fence usage.
requirements.boundary: Vulkan application synchronization remains required. Malformed relocation declarations test kernel trust enforcement, not valid Vulkan application behavior by themselves.

specification.excerpt:
Once written values are made visible to a particular type of memory access,
they can: be read or written by that type of memory access.
Most synchronization commands in Vulkan define a memory dependency.

requirements.requirement: Written values become available and visible to the accesses included in the memory dependency.
requirements.interface: GEM mappings, GART translations, CPU cache maintenance, and completion fences
requirements.test: Retain CPU-to-GPU and GPU-to-CPU producer/consumer digests with completed fences, mapping identity, raw cache controls, and maintenance-on/off controls under the existing hardware procedure.
requirements.boundary: Source ordering and a signaled reservation fence alone do not prove payload visibility or effective snooping.

specification.excerpt:
The first <<synchronization-dependencies-scopes, synchronization scope>>
includes every batch submitted in the same <<devsandqueues-submission, queue
submission>> command.
Fence signal operations that are defined by flink:vkQueueSubmit additionally
include in the first synchronization scope all previous queue submissions to
the same queue via flink:vkQueueSubmit.

requirements.requirement: The fence signal operation follows the submitted batches and the earlier queue operations included in its synchronization scope.
requirements.interface: DRM_RADEON_GEM_WAIT_IDLE on the submission completion BO
requirements.test: Exercise accepted submissions, delayed completion, ioctl refusal, and completion failure through the real queue and kernel seams; verify Vulkan fence state and retained buffer lifetime.
requirements.boundary: Kernel fence publication establishes ordering metadata. Device execution and output validity require separate observations.

specification.excerpt:
Commands that wait indefinitely for device execution (namely
flink:vkDeviceWaitIdle, flink:vkQueueWaitIdle, flink:vkWaitForFences
ifdef::VK_KHR_swapchain[]
or flink:vkAcquireNextImageKHR
endif::VK_KHR_swapchain[]
with a maximum pname:timeout, and flink:vkGetQueryPoolResults with the
ename:VK_QUERY_RESULT_WAIT_BIT bit set in pname:flags) must: return in
finite time even in the case of a lost device, and return either
ename:VK_SUCCESS or ename:VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST.

requirements.requirement: Device loss is terminal for the logical device. Covered indefinite waits return in finite time with VK_SUCCESS or VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST; object handles remain valid for destruction and mapped contents become undefined.
requirements.interface: Submission and wait errno propagation, reservation fence errors, and terminal hardware admission
requirements.test: Inject terminal completion errors through compiled seams and verify finite Vulkan waits, logical-device loss handling, and object teardown. Qualify target recovery separately.
requirements.boundary: A permitted successful wait after device loss does not certify successful GPU output. Exactly-once effects after successful reset remain a separate hardware question.
